message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my SIL (sister-in-law) to "shut up" during dinner. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my SIL has some strong opinions about not watching TV, not listening to pop music, and not having Facebook. She's really proud of these choices and often interrupts conversations to mention them. Instead of just saying she doesn't like something, she makes it about her superiority for not liking it. That's pretty annoying, especially when she does it in front of others. A few days ago, during dinner, my 14-year-old sister started talking about a Marvel movie she watched and was looking forward to the sequel. My SIL jumped in and said she's never watched any Marvel movies and that they seem pretty awful. I got really upset because I don't understand why my SIL feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. I told her loudly to "shut up," adding that not everything has to be about her and what she likes. She blushed and didn't say anything more, and my brother didn't say anything either. But later, he messaged me saying that this was my expression of always hating his wife and that I'm a bad person who doesn't want her to participate in conversations. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by telling her to "shut up." On one hand, she was being rude and dismissive towards my sister, and I felt the need to stand up for her. On the other hand, telling someone to "shut up" is pretty harsh and could be seen as disrespectful, especially in front of others. Plus, my brother took it personally and thinks I'm being mean to his wife. I also need to consider the dynamics of our family. My brother is married to my SIL, and I want to maintain a good relationship with both of them. If I come across as always hating his wife, it could create tension in our family relationships. However, I also don't want to be seen as someone who allows others to be rude or dismissive towards my sister or others. Maybe there's a better way to handle the situation without being so confrontational. Instead of telling her to "shut up," I could have addressed her behavior more calmly or redirected the conversation. But in the moment, I was upset and acted impulsively. I also need to think about the impact of my actions. While I stood up for my sister, I may have hurt my SIL's feelings and strained my relationship with my brother. It's important to balance standing up for what's right with maintaining respectful and harmonious family relationships. Perhaps I should talk to my brother about how I felt in that moment and explain my perspective, while also acknowledging that my choice of words was harsh. This way, we can work towards a better understanding and find healthier ways to handle similar situations in the future. In conclusion, while I felt justified in standing up for my sister, the way I did it by telling my SIL to "shut up" was probably not the best approach. It led to hurt feelings and tension within the family. A more calm and respectful approach would have been better, both for resolving the immediate conflict and for maintaining good relationships in the long run.
